term.english: to listen to / to pay attention

definition: Commonly used to mean 'to pay attention' or 'to obey.' In this context, it describes the act of following one's heart or intuition over logic. It is an essential idiom for expressing whose advice or signals you are prioritizing.

example.spanish: Hace mucho tiempo le hago caso al corazón
example.english: For a long time now I've been listening to my heart

definition: The use of the diminutive suffix '-itos' here is crucial for understanding Spanish emotional nuances. It is not literally about size, but is used to convey extreme affection, tenderness, and intimacy. The phrase 'ojitos lindos' serves as a pet name for the person the singer is enamored with.

example.spanish: Y solo mírame con esos ojito' lindo'
example.english: And just look at me with those pretty little eyes

definition: A colloquial pronunciation of 'enredado' (dropping the 'd'). While it literally means tangled, in a romantic context it describes being emotionally 'caught' or stuck on someone, suggesting a complexity of feelings that is hard to escape.

example.spanish: Pero tú me tiene' enredao, me envolví
example.english: But you have me all tangled up, I got caught up

definition: From the verb 'envolverse' (to wrap oneself up). In Puerto Rican urban slang, this specific reflexive usage means to get deeply infatuated or obsessed with a situation or person, often implies losing one's sense of time or previous intentions because of the intensity of the feeling.

example.spanish: Pero tú me tiene' enredao, me envolví
example.english: But you have me all tangled up, I got caught up

definition: Literally 'asses.' In urban and reggaeton slang, 'un culo' is a crude but common colloquialism used to refer to a person one is dating casually or a romantic interest. Here, Bad Bunny uses it to say he is done with his previous casual hookups to focus on a real connection.

example.spanish: Bye-bye a los culo', ni me despedí
example.english: Bye-bye to the other girls, I didn't even say goodbye

term.english: we collided / ran into each other

definition: Colloquial drop of the 's' from 'chocamos.' While it literally means to crash or collide, in this context it describes a 'destined' encounter—two people whose paths crossed unexpectedly but with high impact, like a physical collision.

term.english: makes me feel / turns me on

definition: A very common colloquial use of 'poner.' It refers to the physical or emotional effect someone has on the speaker. While it can be used to describe arousal, in this song it refers to the unique, intense emotional 'vibe' or state that only this specific partner can trigger.

example.spanish: Nadie me pone como tú me pone'
example.english: No one makes me feel the way you do
